The CLI made our art. We still said no to half of it.

On Tech Thursday, we wired GitHub Copilot CLI to an MCP server that talks directly to our image model. One instruction, and it ran a full batch of brand images on its own -- no clicking through a generator, no manual re-prompting each frame.

The output was fast and it was a lot. It was also, on average, kind of flat. Same thing we're seeing everywhere this week with GPT-6 Astra and Fable 5.1: capability keeps climbing, and taste still isn't automatic.

We kept about half the batch and threw out the rest. That's the part nobody puts in the release notes. Deciding is the actual job now, and it's the part no model does for you.

Here's the sequence: wire the MCP into your CLI environment once. Give it one clear instruction with your real constraints. Generate in batches, not one at a time. Then spend more time discarding than prompting -- discarding is the skill you're actually building.

Agent workflows don't remove judgment. They concentrate it into fewer, sharper decisions.
